item.title: Amid war and sanctions, many Iranians are losing their jobs and struggling to get by
item.description: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.

item.title: The U.S.-Canada trade war is creating a headache for auto-parts makers
item.description: For decades, the U.S. and Canadian auto supply chains have been tightly woven together. The trade war is threatening to unravel a complex system.

item.title: Why gains by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen could push gas prices even higher
item.description: A Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast could help push gas prices up even more as the Iran-backed group also launches attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities.

item.title: Hong Kong court sentences 3 Tiananmen vigil organizers to prison
item.description: The activists were sentenced to about 5 to 7 years in prison in a case widely seen as a barometer of the city's eroding freedoms as Beijing clamps down on dissent.

item.title: Iran-backed Houthi rebels seize a strategic port and island, opening a new battlefront
item.description: The rebel group took over Yemen's port of Mokha, an area vital to controlling shipping through the Red Sea, Houthi and Yemeni officials said. Mokha is about 50 miles from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

item.description: As the U.S. war with Iran drags on, Iranians face increasing layoffs and a rising unemployment rate.

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

item.title: 'I'll never trust them again': Some Afghans who helped the U.S. post-9/11 regret it
item.description: Soon after the Sept. 11 attacks, the U.S. launched what would become a 20-year war in Afghanistan. Some Afghans who helped the U.S. prosecute that war regret it.

item.title: After 900 years, the Bayeux Tapestry returns to England and goes on display in London
item.description: The nearly 230-foot long Bayeux Tapestry is back in England for the first time in 900 years. It depicts the 1066 Battle of Hastings, a turning point in English history that ended Anglo-Saxon rule.
